text: The ratio kcat/Km, which reflects how efficiently an enzyme converts substrate to product, is known as the enzyme's ___ constant.
explanation: kcat/Km is called the specificity constant because it measures catalytic efficiency, especially at low, non-saturating substrate concentrations, and can be used to compare how well an enzyme discriminates between competing substrates. It combines both turnover (kcat) and apparent affinity (1/Km) into a single efficiency measure.
